open_problems.open_problem: Determine the constant-factor minimax MSE scale for one-shot full-GATE estimation on uniform simple d-regular graphs throughout d tending to infinity with d=o(sqrt(n)).

source_refs.claim: The published design-based minimax analysis leaves nonmatching lower and upper risk bounds for full GATE on random regular graphs.
source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje

source_refs.excerpt: proves a d^2/[n log(d+1)] all-procedure lower edge and d^2/n seed-design upper certificate
a different attaining design would remain logically available

open_problems.why_unsolved: The archived runs prove only a logarithmically separated bracket and the retry's seed-union upper-bound argument fails in the dense degree range. The web literature likewise supplies general conflict-graph bounds and a sharper one-sided neighborhood-union result, but not a two-sided full-GATE procedure matching an all-procedure lower bound. Closing the gap requires both a legal observed-data design-estimator pair and a lower bound uniform over outcome-independent assignment laws and possibly biased or randomized estimators.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit scale r(n,d), universal constants c and C, and a graph-dependent assignment law and estimator satisfying c r(n,d) <= R_2(G) <= C r(n,d) with high probability uniformly over all admissible d=o(sqrt(n)).

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the exact decision-theoretic framing and the published random-regular risk interval to be closed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Neighborhood interference obscures global rollout effects -> conflict geometry limits simultaneous endpoint observations -> random regular graphs leave a degree-dependent minimax interval -> identify and attain its sharp scale

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the unrestricted minimax experiment, conflict-graph reduction, and design-adaptive lower-bound construction while replacing coarse graph bounds with balanced two-arm exposure information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its estimand, endpoint-L2 outcome class, random-regular regime, and optimization over all procedures coincide with the desired frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exact exposure probabilities, inverse-probability estimation, and covariance-operator control as the upper-bound template for a new stable-set design.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest implementable full-contrast procedure under unrestricted neighborhood interference.

method_exemplars.technique: Randomize over graph decompositions and integrate full-neighborhood exposure probabilities to avoid persistently unfavorable clusters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an alternative mechanism for overcoming rare full-neighborhood exposures, although not an unrestricted minimax characterization.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a samplable stable-set law for the two-copy full-GATE conflict graph whose normalized treated-control exposure covariance kernel attains the lower-edge risk scale on typical random d-regular graphs.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing stable-set and neighborhood-union constructions control only surrogate or one-sided covariance quantities. Full GATE requires positive treated and control exposure probabilities under one joint assignment, including their cross-arm covariance; naively mixing a design with its complement can create nonvanishing experiment-level covariance. Raw codegree bounds also fail at high overlap even though increased inclusion probabilities may self-normalize that dependence. The missing first step is an exact joint-inclusion calculation for a realizable stable-set law followed by a spectral or Schur bound for its normalized two-arm covariance kernel.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit polynomial-time samplable stable-set law, closed-form pairwise exposure probabilities, a positive-semidefinite covariance-kernel identity, and a high-probability operator bound yielding a full-GATE MSE matching the minimax lower edge up to a universal constant.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing isolates the exposure-denominator versus dependence tradeoff and ends at the unresolved passage from one-sided to full estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bernoulli assignment makes full-neighborhood exposure rare -> neighborhood-union assignment protects one endpoint -> two-sided estimation introduces cross-arm covariance -> design a stable-set law through its normalized covariance kernel

method_exemplars.technique: Resolve incompatible target exposures by randomized priorities and express estimator risk as a quadratic form in the normalized exposure covariance matrix.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed resolution is precisely a sharper covariance-matrix analysis for another realizable conflict-graph law.

method_exemplars.technique: Use an independent focal set and auxiliary assignments to separate focal treatments from their interference exposures, with explicit bias and variance control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Stable focal sets provide the most direct mechanism for realizing compatible treated and control exposure capsules without global-arm dependence.

method_exemplars.technique: Average exposure probabilities over randomized graph decompositions and prove polynomial variance bounds after integrating over decomposition randomness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Randomized decomposition can average heterogeneous local overlap while retaining computable inclusion probabilities.

open_problems.open_problem: Prove a complete-class and strong-duality reduction of the endpoint-L2 full-GATE minimax experiment to a finite convex saddle over realizable stable-set laws and estimator representers.

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the sign-schedule extreme-point reduction ... by an ellipsoidal complete-class ... reduction.
The two programs attain equal optimal objectives.
The exact finite programs can be exponentially large

open_problems.why_unsolved: The donor finite-saddle result treats a finite bounded-outcome menu for which reduction to sign schedules is available. That proof step fails when nature ranges over two empirical-L2 endpoint balls, irrelevant exposures are unrestricted, and estimators may be biased and nonlinear. Conflict-graph invariance identifies feasible stable sets but does not prove that linear representers or a proposed least-favorable prior form a complete class. Without that result, covariance optimization remains an upper-bound method rather than an exact characterization of minimax risk.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite primal-dual conic program proved equal to R_2(G), with recovery maps for an optimal stable-set distribution and observed-data estimator and a high-probability asymptotic evaluation of its value on uniform random regular graphs.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames minimax risk as a conflict-graph functional while leaving a tractable exact characterization unresolved.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The revealed graph defines a finite decision problem -> feasible observations are encoded by stable sets -> coarse graph bounds do not determine risk -> expose and evaluate the exact ellipsoidal saddle

method_exemplars.technique: Use design-based Riesz representers to formulate the optimal linear estimator and its norm, then prove or refute complete-class equivalence with nonlinear and biased estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems estimate a linear causal functional from design-dependent partial evaluations of a fixed potential-outcome schedule.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt mixed-strategy minimax-design duality and its inference constraints to the stable-set observation channel and ellipsoidal outcome class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a convex mixed-design template, while the new theorem must establish losslessness for the network exposure experiment.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the polynomial-time approximation threshold for full-GATE minimax risk on d-regular interference graphs and construct a certified assignment-estimator compiler attaining that threshold on typical random regular graphs.

source_refs.claim: The minimax characterization involves distributions over maximal independent sets, and computationally efficient risk approximation and attaining procedures remain unresolved.

source_refs.author: Vardis Kandiros, Charilaos Pipis, Constantinos Daskalakis, Christopher Harshaw

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact formulations require distributions over exponentially many stable sets, while maximum-independent-set hardness does not automatically transfer to the specialized two-copy conflict graphs generated by full-GATE exposures. Existing priority and greedy designs are efficient but optimize surrogates and lack a posterior certificate comparable with unrestricted R_2(G). The missing step is either an approximation-preserving reduction for this graph family or a random-regular structural argument that compresses or approximately samples the covariance-optimal stable-set law while keeping optimization and sampling error below the statistical risk scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A hardness-of-approximation factor for R_2(G) on the relevant d-regular exposure-conflict graphs and a polynomial-time randomized compiler returning an assignment sampler, estimator, and computable U(G) with R_2(G) <= U(G) <= alpha(d)R_2(G) with high probability.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly separates information-theoretic risk from the computational barriers created by stable-set representations.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Minimax theory defines the best experiment -> its conflict geometry involves hard stable-set objects -> exhaustive compilation is not deployable -> characterize and attain the efficiently accessible frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Use randomized-priority conflict resolution and exact exposure-probability evaluation as the sampler core, retuned toward covariance-optimal stable-set laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already compiles a conflict graph into a polynomial-time assignment and estimator; the missing guarantee is comparison with unrestricted minimax risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a large focal independent set greedily and quantify the resulting effective sample size and estimator performance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its greedy stable-set construction is an efficient benchmark whose approximation loss can be compared with a computational lower bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt graph-cut or semidefinite relaxations for worst-case GATE risk, adding stable-set realizability and an a posteriori covariance certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates tractable graph-dependent GATE design optimization within a restricted family.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish whether a matched-rate stable-set full-GATE estimator admits a studentized design-based central limit theorem at its minimax normalization on random d-regular graphs.

source_refs.claim: The available neighborhood-union result controls worst-case variance for a one-sided estimator but does not provide full-GATE studentization or a variance estimator and limit law.
source_refs.author: Shuangning Li, Shuangping Li

source_refs.author: Peter M. Aronow, Cyrus Samii

open_problems.why_unsolved: A minimax MSE bound does not imply a Gaussian limit or consistently estimable variance. Stable-set assignments create zero joint inclusion probabilities for incompatible exposure pairs and dependence across overlapping closed neighborhoods. A generic dependency-graph CLT applied through the squared graph can impose degree restrictions too strong at the matched-risk normalization, while standard conservative variance estimators may be too loose to studentize at that scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform design-based CLT at the square-root inverse minimax-risk normalization, together with an observable conservative or ratio-consistent variance estimator whose Wald interval has asymptotically valid coverage over bounded finite-population potential outcomes in a stated random-regular degree regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents assignment, point estimation, covariance control, conservative variance estimation, and confidence intervals as one design-based inferential package.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A network design realizes target exposures -> covariance control yields the optimal point-estimation rate -> practitioners still require uncertainty quantification -> prove studentized inference under the matched-rate stable-set design

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a conservative variance estimator accommodating incompatible exposure pairs and combine covariance bounds with a design-based normal approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the same zero-joint-inclusion inference problem for a different conflict-graph randomization.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply exposure-mapping inverse-probability weights, randomization-based variance bounds, and a local-dependence central limit theorem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The full-GATE estimator is an exposure-weighted finite-population sum, but its stable-set dependence requires a sharper version of this argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on random-graph structure, identify leading covariance terms through graph moments, and prove a network-interference CLT with explicit asymptotic variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Random-regular randomness may convert an irregular exposure covariance kernel into deterministic leading terms beyond worst-case dependency-degree bounds.

literature_map:
Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA) formalize direct, indirect, total, and overall causal effects under interference.
Ugander, Karrer, Backstrom, and Kleinberg (2013) introduce graph-cluster randomization and full-neighborhood exposure probabilities for GATE.
Aronow and Samii (2017, AoAS) provide the general exposure-mapping/IPW framework, randomization variances, and local-dependence asymptotic normality.
Eckles, Karrer, and Ugander (2017, Journal of Causal Inference) emphasize design-driven bias reduction under incompletely modeled network interference.
Basse and Airoldi (2018, Sociological Methodology) show that unbiasedness under interference does not by itself ensure concentration.
Leung (2022, Econometrica) develops network-interference CLTs and network-HAC inference under approximate neighborhood interference.
Li and Wager (2022, Annals of Statistics) use random-graph asymptotics to sharpen interference rates and derive explicit limit laws.
Ugander and Yin (2023, Journal of Causal Inference) randomize graph decompositions to replace exponential metric-growth variance behavior with polynomial bounds.
Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi (2024, ICLR) use an independent focal set and auxiliary assignments to separate own-treatment and interference control.
Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw (2024, arXiv:2411.10908) introduce conflict graphs, modified HT estimation, spectral variance bounds, and conservative confidence intervals.
Viviano (2026 revision, arXiv:2003.08421) optimizes participation and assignment using pilot-estimated covariance functions with inference and oracle-regret guarantees.
Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje (2026, arXiv:2608.04909) derive design-based minimax bounds and expose an unresolved random-regular full-GATE frontier.
Li and Li (2026 IMSI slides) obtain a sharper rate for a one-sided neighborhood-union estimator under controlled codegrees while leaving full estimation and intermediate overlap unresolved.
Weinstein and Nevo (2026, Biometrics; arXiv:2302.11322) identify exposure-probability divergence as a robustness axis not yet incorporated into minimax network design.
prior_proposal_map:
The failed exp_randomregular_fullgate_minimax_frontier/v1 and matched_frontier_retry lineages were mined first, including both READMEs, proto_core files, writeups, state files, and angle0 reviewer JSONs.
The v1 archive proves only the logarithmic bracket d^2/[n log(d+1)] below and d^2/n above; review_rubric.json records the unmatched frontier explicitly.
The retry isolates its failed seed-design route to a dense signed four-root reachability moment and records direct Schur-covariance or a different attaining design as live alternatives.
angle0_v4.json supplies the strongest prescriptive route: develop the direct Schur-covariance fallback as a separately named graph-computable target.
The current qid has state and pipeline metadata but no completed proposal core or reviewer JSON; its topic explicitly selects the stable-set exposure covariance kernel and presolve capsule.
Downgraded exp_boundedcluster_endpoint_orbit_minimax/v1 supplies the verified reduction of feasible unrestricted-ANI designs to distributions over realizable independent sets.
Downgraded exp_exposure_ambiguity_design_frontier/v1 supplies the finite-saddle donor, but its bounded-menu sign-schedule reduction and exponential programs do not directly handle endpoint-L2 balls.
